fact: Quest givers should display an icon overhead (!, ?, ★) visible from 20-30 units away. Color coding: yellow=available, gray=not yet available (level requirement), green=in progress, white=completed.
Quest objectives use a step-based structure: fetch X items, reach location, defeat Y enemies, talk to NPC, escort target, defend point, collect loot from specific enemy type.
Quest journals track: quest name, description, current step, reward preview (XP, gold, item). Good UX shows active step highlighted, completed steps crossed out.
Breadcrumb waypoints: a glowing trail or compass marker always points toward current objective. Players should never have to open a map just to find the quest objective.
Side quests vs main quests: main story quests use distinct color (gold/orange), side quests use different color (blue/white). Players can see at a glance what's story-critical.
Quest rewards should appear as an animated chest-open or overlay popup showing items flying toward the HUD slots. Sound: fanfare + item pickup sounds layered.
Branching quests: player choices affect outcome. Store choice flags in a quest state object. Multiple endings require different NPC dialogue trees and different final rewards.
Quest timers for timed missions: show a countdown bar on HUD during time-sensitive quests. Flash red when under 25% time remaining. Play a warning sound at 30 seconds.
Nearby quest tracking: show a small indicator when the player enters a zone where a quest objective exists, even if not currently tracked.
NPC dialogue triggers when player is within 3-5 units and presses interact key (E/F/triangle). Show a floating 'Press E to talk' prompt that fades in as player approaches.
Dialogue UI: show speaker portrait (left or right), speaker name, dialogue text with typewriter effect at 40-60 chars/sec. Player response options appear below after text completes.
NPC conversation cameras: cut to a close-up shot of the NPC's face during dialogue. Use a slow dolly-in for important story moments. Return to gameplay camera on dialogue end.
Response option system: show 2-4 responses the player can choose. Label options by tone: [Aggressive], [Friendly], [Question], [Leave]. Affects NPC relationship score.
NPC relationship system: track relationship score per NPC (-100 to +100). High relationship unlocks unique dialogue, quests, discounts at merchants, or romance options.
Idle NPC behavior: NPCs not in dialogue should wander a small area, look at the player when nearby, perform ambient animations (cleaning, reading, sharpening sword).
Merchant NPCs open a shop UI on dialogue end. Shop has categories: weapons, armor, consumables, misc. Highlight affordable items in white, unaffordable in gray.
Quest-giving dialogue: NPC explains the problem, player accepts or declines. On accept: quest added to journal, NPC says goodbye line, quest marker appears on map.
Voiced vs text dialogue: if using text only, animate the NPC mouth or use body language (nodding, gesturing) to imply they're speaking. Silence feels wrong.
NPC memory: NPCs should remember past interactions. If player completed their quest, they say 'Thanks for your help!' not the same intro line.
Inventory grid: items occupy 1x1 to 3x3 slots. Show item icon, quantity (stack count bottom-right), rarity color border (gray=common, green=uncommon, blue=rare, purple=epic, orange=legendary).
Inventory capacity: weight-based or slot-based. Weight: each item has kg value, player has max carry weight shown as bar. Slot: fixed grid (like Resident Evil 4 attache case).
Item tooltip on hover: show item name, type, stats comparison (+/- vs equipped), description, sell value, weight. Use green for better than equipped, red for worse.
Quick slot bar (hotbar): 8-10 slots on bottom of screen. Player drags items from inventory to hotbar. Press 1-8 or D-pad to use. Show cooldown overlay on slot when used.
Equipment slots: head, chest, legs, feet, hands, ring (x2), necklace, weapon (main hand), offhand/shield. Show mannequin or character silhouette with slots highlighted.
Loot pickup: auto-pickup for small items when player walks over them. Large items require interact. Show a loot bag icon when enemy dies with items inside.
Inventory sorting: sort by type, by rarity, by value, or manually. Drag-and-drop to rearrange. Right-click for context menu: equip, drop, sell, split stack, examine.
Item stacking: consumables and materials stack up to 99 or 999. Weapons and armor are unique (do not stack). Show stack count as number overlay on item icon.
Trash/drop system: drag item to a trash slot or press delete key. Show confirmation popup for rare+ items: 'Drop [Epic Sword]? Yes / No'. Prevent accidental loss.
Chest and container looting: open container shows a split-screen: left=container contents, right=player inventory. 'Take All' button at top. Individual items can be dragged over.
Save slots: show 3-10 save slots as cards with: screenshot thumbnail, character name, level, location name, playtime, date saved. Most recent save is highlighted.
Autosave: trigger on: entering new area, after major quest milestone, every 5-10 minutes. Show a small save icon (floppy disk or cloud) in corner for 2 seconds when autosave triggers.
Checkpoint saves (soulslike): save points are physical objects in the world (bonfires, statues, benches). Player must manually rest/activate. All enemies respawn on rest.
Save data structure: store player position (x,y,z), rotation, current HP/stamina, inventory array, equipped items, quest states object, NPC relationship scores, discovered areas map, playtime.
Quick save / quick load: F5 to quick save, F9 to quick load. Show 'SAVED' text in corner on quick save. Quick load shows a 1-second black flash then continues.
Load screen: show a world/location image as background, loading bar at bottom, rotating game logo, and a gameplay tip that changes every few seconds.
Save corruption prevention: write to a temp file first, verify integrity, then rename to final save file. Keep one backup save. Show error if save fails with retry option.
Cloud saves: sync to cloud automatically when game exits. Show cloud sync status in save menu. Allow choosing between local and cloud version if they conflict.
New game vs continue: main menu shows 'Continue' (last save) prominently if a save exists. 'New Game' prompts difficulty selection and character customization.
Main menu structure: [Continue / Load Game] [New Game] [Multiplayer] [Settings] [Credits] [Quit]. Most common action (Continue) is always at top.
Main menu background: animated scene from the game world (camera slowly panning through a forest, city street, dungeon corridor). Show the game's atmosphere immediately.
Main menu audio: ambient game music plays (dramatic, calm, or action depending on game tone). Fade in on menu load. Music loops seamlessly.
New game flow: difficulty selection → character name/appearance → optional backstory/class choice → brief intro cinematic → world load.

Settings menu sections: Graphics (resolution, quality, vsync, FOV), Audio (master/music/SFX/voice volume), Controls (key rebinding, sensitivity, invert Y), Accessibility (colorblind mode, subtitles, text size).
Pause menu (in-game): ESC opens overlay with [Resume] [Save Game] [Load Game] [Settings] [Main Menu]. Blur the game world behind the pause menu. Resume instantly on click.
Death screen: show a dramatic death animation, then fade to a red-tinted screen. Options: [Respawn at Checkpoint] [Load Last Save] [Main Menu]. Show how player died.
Game over vs death: death = respawn at nearby checkpoint. Game over = mission failed, restart mission. Distinguish clearly with different UI and messaging.
Character creation: sliders for facial features, body type, skin tone (full spectrum), hair style/color, starting outfit. Preview character in 3D rotating view.
Core HUD elements: health bar (top-left), stamina/energy bar (below health), minimap (top-right), hotbar (bottom-center), crosshair (center), objective text (top-center).
Health bar design: red fill, shows current/max HP as number, animate damage as red flash then drain. Low health (<25%): pulse red, add heartbeat sound, vignette around screen edges.
Stamina bar: yellow or green, depletes on sprint/dodge/attack, regens after brief delay. Show depletion flash when empty. Hide bar when full to reduce clutter.
Minimap: circular, shows player (center, rotating arrow), nearby enemies (red dots), quest waypoints (colored markers), discovered POIs (icons). Click to open full map.
Damage numbers: floating text appears at hit location showing damage dealt. Color-code: white=normal, yellow=critical, purple=poison, blue=frost, red=fire. Scale number by damage amount.
Notification feed (top-right or bottom-left): short text notifications stack up and fade out. 'Quest Updated', 'Item Acquired', 'Achievement Unlocked', 'Level Up'. Each lasts 3-4 seconds.
Compass bar: horizontal bar across top showing cardinal directions and quest markers as colored icons. More intuitive than minimap for open-world navigation.
Contextual prompts: when near an interactable object, show 'Press E to [action]' near the object. Fade in on approach, fade out on leaving. Don't clutter at all times.
Boss health bar: appears at bottom of screen when boss is engaged. Shows boss name, phase indicator (e.g. 'Phase 2'), health bar that drains dramatically.
Crafting UI: show a 3x3 or 4x4 grid of ingredient slots, arrow pointing right, result item slot. Place ingredients to see what gets crafted. Match recipe exactly.
Recipe discovery: auto-unlock recipes when player acquires all needed materials for first time. Recipe book stores all discovered recipes with ingredients listed.
Upgrade crafting: take existing weapon/armor, add upgrade materials, increase +1 to +10. Show stat improvement preview before confirming. Cost increases with each upgrade level.
Workbench vs inventory crafting: simple recipes craftable anywhere (bandages from cloth). Complex recipes need a workbench, forge, or alchemy table. Mark required station on recipe.
Material gathering: ores from rocks (mining animation), wood from trees (chopping animation), herbs from glowing plants (picking animation). Each has a short interact animation.
Crafting feedback: show crafting animation on workbench (hammering, mixing, stitching). On completion: item flies to inventory slot with sparkle effect and sound.
Skill tree layout: radial (branching from center) or linear (left to right) or constellation style. Each node is a skill icon, connected by lines. Locked nodes are darkened.
XP and leveling: kill enemies for XP, complete quests for larger XP chunks. Fill XP bar → level up → flash/fanfare → gain skill points to spend in tree.
Skill types: passive (permanent stat boosts), active (new abilities mapped to buttons), combo (modify existing moves with new properties).
Skill prerequisites: must unlock parent skill before child is available. Show the connection lines and indicate what's needed. Highlight the path to desired skill.
Attribute points: STR (carry weight, melee damage), DEX (attack speed, crit chance), VIT (max HP), INT (spell power, crafting quality), AGI (movement speed, dodge distance).
Respec system: allow resetting skill points for a cost (gold or rare item). Players should be able to experiment without permanent mistakes.
World map: opens with M key. Shows full world with fog of war (unexplored=dark). Discovered areas reveal terrain, roads, settlements. Fast travel points shown as icons.
Map markers: player can place custom markers (right-click on map). Built-in markers: quests (★), shops (bag icon), dungeons (skull), save points (campfire), bosses (crown).
Zone map vs world map: world map for overall navigation, zone map for detailed interior layout (dungeon floor plan, city district). Toggle with zoom or separate key.
Points of Interest (POIs): shown as icons on map when discovered. Types: ruins, cave, camp, viewpoint, shrine, merchant. Undiscovered POIs have ? marks until found.
Minimap vs full map: minimap always visible in corner (small, rotates with player). Full map pauses game and shows everything. Both update in real-time as player explores.
Fast travel: click discovered fast travel point on map → black screen transition → appear at destination. Only available when not in combat or danger.
Dynamic music system: music changes based on situation. Exploration = ambient/calm. Combat starts = music transitions to action layer. Combat ends = music fades back to calm over 5-10 seconds.
Spatial audio: sounds have 3D position. Enemies heard from direction they're in. Water sounds louder when closer. Use audio reverb zones: caves echo, outdoors dry, indoors slight reverb.

Footstep variety: different sounds for different surfaces: grass (soft swish), stone (hard click), wood (hollow thud), sand (muffled crunch), metal (ring). Vary pitch randomly ±10% to avoid repetition.
UI sounds: every button click, menu open/close, item pickup, notification, level up has a distinct sound. Keep UI sounds subtle (lower volume than gameplay sounds).
Enemy audio cues: enemies make sounds for: detected player (alert sound), attacking (grunt/swing), taking damage (pain sound), dying (death sound). Player uses these as feedback.
Ambient soundscapes: forest = birds + wind + leaves. City = crowd murmur + distant music + carts. Cave = drips + echo + subtle wind. Layer 2-4 ambient tracks per environment.
Third-person camera: follows player from behind and slightly above (shoulder or overhead). Smooth follow with slight lag. Adjust height when in cover or indoors.
Camera collision: camera should not clip through walls or terrain. Push camera toward player when obstructed. Show player silhouette through walls when camera is blocked.
Lock-on system: press button to lock camera onto nearest enemy. Camera centers on enemy. Strafe around locked target. Release to return to free camera. Useful for boss fights.
Camera shake: apply screen shake on: heavy impacts, explosions, landing from height, taking heavy damage. Short duration (0.2-0.5s), decreasing intensity. Don't overdo it.
FOV settings: let players set FOV (60-110 degrees). Wider FOV for PC (100+). Narrow FOV for cinematic or console. Dynamic FOV: increase slightly during sprint for speed sensation.
Cinematic cameras: for cutscenes and story moments, take control of camera. Use dramatic angles, slow zooms, reaction shots of NPCs. Return to gameplay camera smoothly.
Hit detection feedback: successful hit shows: impact particle effect at hit location, screen flash (brief white or red), damage number, hit sound, enemy reaction animation (flinch).
Block and parry: block reduces damage (50-80%), parry at perfect timing negates all damage and staggers enemy. Parry: bright flash effect, loud metal clang sound, brief slow-motion moment.
Dodge roll: brief invincibility frames during roll (8-16 frames). Show afterimage trail during dodge. Stamina cost per dodge. Can dodge through enemy attacks.
Status effects visual: burning = fire particles on body. Poisoned = green tint + dripping particles. Frozen = ice crystal overlay. Stunned = stars circling head. Each has unique color.
Enemy death: enemies have death animations (fall backward, crumple, explode). Physics-based ragdoll after animation. Drop loot bag visible immediately. Despawn after 30-60 seconds.
Combo system: string light attacks + heavy attacks for combos. Show combo counter HUD element. Each combo has a distinct animation sequence. Final hit has extra impact effect.
Currency types: bronze/silver/gold tiered (100 bronze = 1 silver, 100 silver = 1 gold). Show wallet in HUD during shop. Animate coins when spending/earning.
Shop restock: merchant inventory refreshes daily (in-game time) or after completing quests. Some rare items have limited stock (1-3) and don't restock. Creates urgency.
Buy/sell interface: left side = merchant stock, right side = player inventory. Price shown per item. 'Sell All Junk' button for items tagged as trash. Bargaining skill reduces prices.
Item pricing logic: vendors buy items at 30-50% of value. Players sell for less than they buy. Rare items worth more but harder to sell. Fences buy stolen goods at 20% value.
Loot economy balance: common enemies drop 1-10 coins. Bosses drop 100-500 coins + rare items. Quest rewards = 200-1000 coins. Prices scale with game progression zone.
Contextual tutorials: teach mechanics exactly when they first appear. First time near an enemy: 'Press [attack] to attack'. First time on low health: 'Use a healing item with [hotkey]'.
Tutorial popups: small overlay in corner (not fullscreen). Shows keybind icon + brief instruction. Auto-dismiss after 5 seconds or when player performs the action.
Tutorial skip: let experienced players skip all tutorials at new game start. Remember this preference. Never re-show a tutorial the player has completed.
Tutorial dungeon/area: optional starting area that teaches all basic mechanics in a safe environment. Gate it behind a choice: 'I need help' or 'I know how to play'.
Visual highlighting: during tutorials, highlight the relevant UI element or world object with a golden glow or arrow pointing to it. Removes once player interacts.
Achievement types: story milestones (unmissable, bronze), side activities (optional, silver), mastery challenges (grind, gold/platinum). Show total completion percentage.
Achievement popup: appear in corner (top-right). Show achievement icon, name, and description. Brief fanfare sound. Disappears after 4-5 seconds. Can stack if multiple unlock at once.
Achievement menu: grid of achievement cards. Locked = silhouette + ???. Unlocked = full icon + unlock date. Progress achievements show bar (e.g. 'Kill 100/500 enemies').
Secret achievements: shown as ??? in menu until unlocked. Rewards curiosity. After unlocking, full description reveals retroactively.
Lobby screen: shows all connected players with their: character avatar, name, level, ready status checkmark. Host has crown icon. Character load screen visible to all players.
Matchmaking flow: Quick Match → searching spinner with player count → found lobby → waiting for players → countdown timer → game start.
Lobby chat: text chat panel in lobby. Players type messages. Emote buttons for quick reactions. Mute individual players. Report player option.
Session code: host generates a 6-character code. Friends enter code to join directly (skip matchmaking). Show code prominently in lobby UI.
In-game HUD for multiplayer: show all players' health bars (small) in corner. Player nameplates float above characters. Scoreboard accessible via Tab key.
Drop-in/drop-out co-op: host can enable co-op mid-game. Joining players spawn at host location. If player drops, game continues without them. Enemies scale by player count.
Locomotion blend tree: idle → walk → run → sprint all blend smoothly based on movement speed. Blend time: 0.1-0.2 seconds. Strafe animations for left/right movement.
Root motion vs in-place: root motion = animation moves character position (more realistic). In-place = code moves character, animation plays in place (more controllable).
IK (Inverse Kinematics): feet plant on uneven terrain (foot IK). Hands grip weapon realistically (hand IK). Eyes look at player or points of interest (look-at IK).
Ragdoll death: on death, switch from death animation to physics ragdoll. Ragdoll takes velocity from last hit direction. Character tumbles naturally. Prop ragdolls for barrels, boxes.
Facial animations: use blend shapes for facial expressions. Angry, happy, sad, surprised, neutral. Trigger during dialogue or combat reactions. NPCs look alive, not robotic.
Weapon animations: each weapon type has unique attack animations. Sword: slash sets. Bow: draw-hold-release. Magic: casting pose with particle buildup. Gun: recoil + reload.
Destructible objects: wooden crates, barrels, fences, glass windows shatter when hit. Use pre-fractured meshes that break into pieces. Physics on pieces for 2-3 seconds then despawn.
Pushable objects: heavy boxes or carts can be pushed by player. Use physics joints and mass. Player push animation plays. Object slides along ground with friction sound.
Water physics: player wades when water depth is knee-height (slowed movement). Swims when deeper. Submerging triggers underwater audio filter (muffled). Breath meter if underwater too long.
Climbing and ledge grab: when player approaches a ledge at correct height and speed, auto-grab. Pull-up animation plays. Can hang and shimmy left/right. Drop when pressing down.
Throwable items: player can pick up (F) small physics objects and throw (LMB). Object follows projectile arc. Deals damage on hit to enemies. Breaks on impact with hard surfaces.

Time of day cycle: 24-hour cycle (compressed to 15-30 real minutes). Dawn: golden low-angle light from east. Noon: harsh overhead light, short shadows. Dusk: orange-red sky. Night: dark, moon/stars, artificial lights glow.

Interior lighting: candles and torches flicker (randomize intensity ±10% every frame). Windows cast shaft-of-light beams. Dungeons: sparse torchlight leaves deep shadows. Creates atmosphere and tension.
Weather effects: rain = particles falling + ground splash particles + wet material on surfaces + fog increase + ambient sound. Snow = white particles + accumulation on surfaces + footprints.
Fog of war in top-down games: black overlay on unexplored areas. Explored but not visible = dark gray overlay. Currently visible = full color. Units have sight radius that reveals around them.
Danger zones: red tint on screen edges when in combat or danger. Dark vignette for horror/stealth sections. Green tint briefly after healing. Blue tint in cold areas.

Industrial/horror aesthetic (Ill-style): flickering fluorescent lights, pools of oil reflecting light, steam venting from pipes, oppressive concrete walls, single exposed bulb lighting in small rooms, darkness beyond 15 units.
Dungeon entrance: always marked with a distinctive visual (stone archway, cave mouth, iron door, grate). Nearby text prompt or signpost tells player what lies within (dungeon name, suggested level).
Dungeon rooms: procedural or hand-crafted. Key room types: combat arena, puzzle room, trap corridor, treasure room, boss chamber, safe room (no enemies, save point).
Dungeon lighting: torches every 8-10 units along corridors. Boss rooms often have dramatic overhead lighting (skylight shaft or magical light source). Dead ends are darker than main paths.
Dungeon navigation: leave subtle breadcrumbs so players don't get completely lost: vines growing toward exits, airflow indicating outside, sound of water showing level transitions.
Trap systems: pressure plates (step triggers), tripwires (walking triggers), proximity triggers (approach triggers). Visual telegraphing: plates are slightly different color, wires glint in light.
Dungeon verticality: use multiple levels connected by stairs, ladders, drop-down ledges, elevators. Falling damage applies beyond 5 units drop height. Roll on landing reduces damage.
Boss room design: large circular or square arena with clear boundaries. Environmental hazards (lava pit edges, crushers). Multiple exits from the boss fight once defeated.
